### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

> "The subscription year on his energy programme finishes at the end of this month, and what he rings about is the savings guarantee … He wants the guarantee settled and the money that is owed under it paid out to Cedarhurst now, before the year closes, and he says so plainly at the start."
> "He is content for the desk to work through whatever records it needs and to act for him on the company's side of it, and he is not asking to cancel anything, to renew anything or to change what the programme covers."
> "Asked what he thinks he is owed, he says he has not worked it out and does not intend to, that it is the company's figure to produce, and he will not put a number to it."

- Target object: the savings guarantee on the one energy programme at the Medical Pavilion ("it is the only one on the energy programme").
- Timing: now, before the year closes (the term ends 2026-09-30).
- Boundary: settle and pay the guarantee; no cancellation, no renewal, no change of cover.
- Authorisation mode: the desk acts on the company's side; the **customer alone** performs the one write that commits him to money — "then does the authorisation himself when it is handed to him, using exactly the figures the desk gives him."

The simulator is passive: it volunteers the retrofit fact only when asked ("Asked whether anything changed at the building over the year, he says they put two new chillers in over the winter and the work was signed off in the spring, and he leaves it there unless he is asked more"), refuses to supply any number or method ("He does not know how the guarantee is worked out and never proposes a method, a period or an order of doing anything"), and reacts to the coverage amendment only after the desk raises it ("When the desk tells him that the points the building now meters have to be carried on the programme before the year can be settled … he grumbles … accepts the answer he is given and then does the authorisation himself when it is handed to him"). It states no policy and no expected value. His account of the chillers is not authority: *Desk Guidance — Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions and the Building's Other Cover* — "the owner's description of the works does not stand in for the record."

### 4. Each scored parameter, its formula in words, inputs, intermediates and value

Tier figures for the Measurement & Verification Program, all read from the visible tier tables: annual subscription fee 34 000, annual fee per included meter 165, meter overage fee 130, gateway fee 480, included interval meters 30, included dashboard users 30, dashboard user fee 130, escalation at renewal 3.0 percent, billing monthly on 45-day terms, baseline period 24 calendar months, weather normalised **yes**, true-up **annual**, baseline reset on retrofit **yes**, guaranteed reduction **8 percent**, annual guarantee ceiling **USD 45 000**, shortfall share **75 percent**, rate structure kept current **yes**, demand response support **yes**.

#### (a) The amended annual fee — *Pricing Desk Statement — The Amended Annual Fee*

Baseline: "the fee the amendment is struck on, plus the per-point fee for every point the subscription covers after the amendment, plus the charge for the points beyond the tier's included count, plus the charge for the dashboard users beyond the tier's included count, plus the data gateway charge; the five parts are added and the total is rounded to the nearest cent once at the end."

**The points the site meters** = "the metered points that posted a reading in the month ending on the day of the amendment, one reading to a point" → the 34 distinct interval meters MTR-500211 … MTR-500244, each with one reading posted 2026-09-05, inside the month ending 2026-09-17. **34 points.**

*(Boundary recorded, not resolved: the utility-bill account MTR-500100 also posted a reading on 2026-09-05. I read it as not one of "the points the site meters", because the corpus elsewhere separates the two record kinds by name and because the coverage-share rule below — "at least one for every point covered" — resolves cleanly at 34 and not at 35. The amended-fee and per-point-band documents do not themselves name the reading source, so I record this as an openness on the visible surface; at 35 points the fee would be USD 42 092.50 and the coverage share 95 percent instead.)*

| Part | Rule document and limb reached | Evidence from the records | Value |

| Users beyond | *Dashboard Users Beyond the Included Count* — "6 or more | 12 or more | the tier's dashboard user fee less 10 percent" | `dashboard_users 37` − 30 included = 7; term run 2023-10-01 → 35 whole months | 130 × 0.9 = 117.00; × 7 = **819.00** |
| Data gateway | *The Data Gateway Charge* — "active or pending renewal | more than one source | the tier's gateway fee less 50 percent" | plan `status 'active'`; subscription `data_source 'mixed'` | 480 × 0.5 = **240.00** |

Baseline: "The reset baseline is the measured basis less the reduction the new plant accounts for; that reduction is the measured basis multiplied by the equipment share, then by the retrofit reduction, then by the running share, and the figure that remains is taken down to the whole kilowatt hour."

| Billed window | *The Billed Electricity Window behind a Baseline Reset* — "more than 12 months | any | the billed readings of the tier's baseline period, that total multiplied by 12 and divided by the number of months in that period" | tier baseline period 24 months; the 24 utility-bill readings posted 2024-10-05 … 2026-09-05 total 12 × 560 000 + 6 × 545 000 + 6 × 430 000 = 12 570 000 kWh | 12 570 000 × 12 ÷ 24 = **6 285 000 kWh** |
| Equipment share | *The Equipment Share of a Baseline Reset* — "chiller replacement … | 46 percent" | `scope_summary 'chiller_replacement'` on the closed project | **46 percent** |
| Retrofit reduction | *The Retrofit Reduction by Project Value* — "USD 1000000 or more | 22 percent" | `contract_value_usd 1480000.0` | **22 percent** |

Reduction = 6 285 000 × 0.46 = 2 891 100; × 0.22 = 636 042; × 5 ÷ 12 = 265 017.5.
**Reset baseline = 6 285 000 − 265 017.5 = 6 019 982.5, taken down to the whole kilowatt hour = 6 019 982 kWh.**

`billing_period` for the verification and the payment is **`2026`**, the whole subscription year: the tier trues up annually, the year closes 2026-09-30, and the records use exactly that spelling — `energy_guarantee_credited` carries `billing_period '2026'` and the previous `energy_savings_verified` / `energy_shortfall_paid` pair carries `'2025'`.

1. `verify_customer_identity(customer_id, account_number='640751', tax_id_last4='4468')` — agent-owned.
2. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool('authorise_meter_coverage_01d41e30')`, then the **customer** runs `call_user_discoverable_tool('authorise_meter_coverage_01d41e30', {subscription_id, meters_covered: 34, annual_fee_usd: 41820.40})`. Owner fixed by the card: "the building owner's own tool, because the amendment commits them to a higher annual fee: the client services agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it, on their own authority." The persona matches exactly.
3. `charge`-free agent write: `reset_performance_baseline_0e66b991(subscription_id, baseline_kwh = 6019982)` — agent-owned.
4. `verify_period_savings_a6d7fa6e(subscription_id, customer_id, site_id, billing_period='2026', verified_savings_usd=15722.66, guaranteed_savings_usd=57791.83, weather_normalized='true')` — agent-owned.
5. `pay_savings_shortfall_2f1bc21a(subscription_id, customer_id, billing_period='2026', amount_usd=9475.14)` — agent-owned.

Forward/backward dependencies: 2 → 3 → 4 → 5, each strictly ordered (see item 6); the terminal state is the payment standing on the subscription's guarantee record for 2026, which is what the caller asked to hear ("Once he hears that the payment against the guarantee has been made and what it came to").

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer asked for **one** thing: the guarantee settled and paid.

**Problem A — pay the owner against the savings guarantee (the root).**
*Desk Tool Card — Paying a Building Owner against the Savings Guarantee* carries one sentence saying what its result waits on:

> "The shortfall paid against the guarantee is worked out only after a signed-off verification of the measured savings for the true-up period stands on the subscription's record."

Form: **state** — a record-visible state, no tool, no performer, no route.
**Does it hold?** No. `find_energy_events` shows exactly one `energy_savings_verified` row, `billing_period '2025'`, `verified_date '2025-11-20'`. The true-up period he is asking about is the year that closes 2026-09-30 (the tier trues up annually; the guarantee credited for it carries `billing_period '2026'`). No verification for that period stands.
**Finding the write:** searching the words the sentence and the records use — "verification", "savings verified", "true-up", "signed off" — reaches *Desk Tool Card — Signing Off a True-Up on an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription*, which states its own rule in the same words: "At the tier's true-up the measured savings of the closing period are verified against the baseline standing on the subscription, and the figure signed off is what the guarantee is settled on. The verification is entered on the subscription's record for the period named, dated the day it is signed off." Hop mark: **state-derived**.

**Problem B — sign off the true-up for the closing period.**
Its own document carries:

> "The savings verified for a true-up period are worked out only after the baseline standing on the subscription has been restated from the close of the replacement or retrofit project at the building."

Form: **state**.
**Does it hold?** No. The subscription still carries `baseline_kwh 6480000` with `baseline_start_date '2021-10-01'` / `baseline_end_date '2023-09-30'` — the original 24-month window before the term start — while `find_retrofit_projects` shows a project `status 'closed'`, `completion_date '2026-03-20'` at the same site. `last_change_type` on the subscription reads `'users_added'`, dated 2026-04-14: no baseline reset is stamped on the record. And *Desk Guidance — The Subscription and the Building's Other Cover* independently makes the reset due: "Where a retrofit project at the same building reaches completion and the tier resets the baseline on retrofit, the baseline is reset from the project's completion date"; the tier resets on retrofit (*Savings Guarantee and Measurement Terms Annex*, clause 8).
**Finding the write:** searching "baseline", "restated", "retrofit closed" reaches *Desk Tool Card — Restating the Performance Baseline*: "When a replacement or retrofit project at the building closes and the tier resets its baseline on retrofit, the performance baseline the subscription measures against is restated … replacing the baseline standing on the subscription with the annual electricity figure entered." Hop mark: **state-derived**.

**Problem C — restate the performance baseline.**
Its own document carries:

> "The reset baseline is fixed only once the metered points the subscription covers match the points the site meters."

Form: **state**.
**Does it hold?** No. `meters_covered 30` on the subscription against 34 distinct interval meters that posted a reading in the month ending on the day (MTR-500211 … MTR-500244, posted 2026-09-05). The two do not match.
**Finding the write:** searching "metered points", "covers", "taken onto the subscription" reaches *Customer Authorisation Card — Taking Metered Points onto an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription*: "When a building owner authorises the metered points their site actually meters to be taken onto an energy monitoring subscription, the subscription's annual fee is restated for the points and dashboard users it then covers. The covered point count and the annual fee standing on the subscription both change." Hop mark: **state-derived**.

**Problem D — authorise the metered points onto the subscription (the customer's own write).** Its documents carry no prerequisite sentence of their own. The tree terminates.

**Resulting tree, direction and order:**

```
D  authorise the metered points onto the subscription   (customer-owned write)
      │  D before C
      ▼
C  restate the performance baseline                     (agent-owned write)
      │  C before B
      ▼
B  sign off the true-up for the closing period          (agent-owned write)
      │  B before A
      ▼
A  pay the owner against the savings guarantee          (agent-owned write, the root the caller raised)
```

Handling order: D, C, B, A. Every hop is **state-derived**; **no hop is pre-solved** — no document named another problem's tool, stated a route, or aggregated the chain. Each blocked document says only what its own result waits on, in a record-visible state, and the write that brings the state about had to be found from the depended-on document's own rule and from the records.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure above is a tool return or a published sentence quoted verbatim.

**Closest alternatives, and what excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | Excluded by |
|---|---|
| Strike the amendment on the plain annual fee 34 000 | *The Fee an Amendment of Coverage is Struck On*, "pending renewal | the tier's annual subscription fee escalated once at the tier's escalation rate"; `status 'pending_renewal'` |
| Per-point fee at the full 165 | *Per-Point Fee Bands*, "21 through 60 | that fee less 6 percent"; 34 covered points |
| Charge the whole gateway fee 480 | *The Data Gateway Charge*, "active or pending renewal | more than one source | the tier's gateway fee less 50 percent"; `data_source 'mixed'` and the plan active |
| Take the measured basis as the baseline standing (6 480 000) | *The Measured Basis of a Baseline Reset*, "the utility bills alone, or more than one source | any | the billed electricity gathered over the window" |
| Take the last 12 billed months, or the last 6 taken twice | *The Billed Electricity Window behind a Baseline Reset*, first row: the tier fixes its baseline over 24 months, "more than 12 months" |
| Equipment share 100 percent / reduction 8 percent | *The Equipment Share of a Baseline Reset* ("chiller replacement … 46 percent") and *The Retrofit Reduction by Project Value* ("USD 1000000 or more | 22 percent"); the closed project is a chiller replacement of USD 1 480 000 |
| Running share 100 percent | *The Running Share of a New Plant*, "12 or fewer | annual | those months, of 12"; 5 whole months since 2026-03-20 |
| Unit cost over 24 months | *The Unit Cost Savings are Valued At*, "yes | yes | the average of the billed readings of the last 12 months"; the tier keeps the rate structure current and a bill was posted 2026-09-05 |
| Weather share 100 percent, attributed 100 percent, coverage 85 percent | the three schedules' own rows, against `repair_allowance_remaining 0.0` on an active agreement, 12 billed readings in the window, and 34 covered points at or above the 30 included |
| Measured shortfall totalled over every verification on record | *Measuring a Guarantee Shortfall*, "annual | the latest verification standing on the subscription"; the tier trues up annually |
| System share 100 percent, paid share 75 percent, year share the whole year | the three schedules' rows, against `support_hours_remaining 0.0` on an active plan, one shortfall paid on 2026-02-10, and a project closed 5 whole months ago at a tier that resets on retrofit |
| Hold the payment to the whole guaranteed figure, or pay with no offset | *The Guarantee Standing behind a Shortfall Payment* ("above nothing | one or more | the credited total less the payments made in those months") and *Amounts Owed Set Against a Shortfall Payment* ("active or pending renewal | above nothing | …"); `balance_due 3285.84` |
| Pay by cheque | he "does not ask for a cheque"; the tool takes no payment method |
| Refuse the claim as a change outside the company's control | the only change on record is the company's own closed project; *Guarantee Terms Commentary* names "occupancy hours, added equipment or a change of tenant" |
| The desk performs the coverage amendment itself | *Customer Authorisation Card*: "the building owner's own tool … the customer themselves runs it, on their own authority" |

One boundary is left open on the visible surface and is recorded rather than closed: whether the utility-bill account counts among "the points the site meters" (item 4(a)).

**Counter-proof against "he asked for one thing, so do only that one thing."** Paying the guarantee straight away is impossible on the visible surface: the payment document's own sentence says the shortfall "is worked out only after a signed-off verification of the measured savings for the true-up period stands on the subscription's record", and `find_energy_events` shows no verification for the closing period. Signing one off is in turn blocked — "The savings verified for a true-up period are worked out only after the baseline standing on the subscription has been restated from the close of the replacement or retrofit project at the building" — and the subscription still carries its pre-term baseline while a closed project sits on the site's record. Restating is blocked in turn — "The reset baseline is fixed only once the metered points the subscription covers match the points the site meters" — and 30 covered points stand against 34 metered. Each exclusion is a visible sentence read against a visible record; none is a pointer, a tool name or a route.

**Counter-proof on the calculations — the fall-back numbers.** Reading each computation document alone, with the product figures it names and no factor applied:

- *The Amended Annual Fee*: 34 000 + 34 × 165 + 4 × 130 + 7 × 130 + 480 = **USD 41 520.00** (against 41 820.40).
- *Working Out a Reset Performance Baseline*: measured basis "the baseline standing on the subscription" 6 480 000; equipment share 100 percent; retrofit reduction 8 percent; running share 100 percent → reduction 518 400 → **5 961 600 kWh** (against 6 019 982).
- *Valuing the Measured Savings of a True-Up Period*: saved electricity "a quarter of the baseline … less the electricity the period's readings recorded over the three months ending on the day of the verification, that difference taken four times" → a quarter of 5 961 600 is 1 490 400, less 3 × 430 000 = 1 290 000, leaves 200 400, taken four times = 801 600 kWh; unit cost the 24-month average 1 470 000 ÷ 12 570 000 = USD 0.1169…; shares 100 / 100 / 85 → a definite figure near **USD 79 600**, and savings guaranteed 8 percent of 5 961 600 valued at the same cost.
- *The Shortfall Paid*: measured shortfall "totalled over every verification standing on the subscription"; system share 100 percent; paid share the tier's 75 percent; guarantee standing "the guaranteed savings standing on the subscription"; year share the whole year; "No offset is taken off the payment" → a definite figure, and in every case different from USD 9475.14.

All four fall-backs are computable and definite, and every product figure the four baselines name (tier annual fee, per-meter fee, overage fee, user fee, gateway fee, included counts, the standard reduction 8 percent, the guaranteed share, the ceiling and the shortfall share) is rendered somewhere in the corpus.

**A source-layer note recorded during the blind phase (not a verdict).** *Pricing Desk Note — Portfolio Meter Pricing* states, under the heading "Basis in force": "The annual fee of a subscription is the tier's annual subscription fee, plus the tier's per-meter fee multiplied by the meters the subscription covers, plus the tier's meter overage fee multiplied by the meters covered beyond the tier's included count …, plus the tier's data gateway fee, the total rounded to the nearest cent." **On the one open boundary (a policy-side note, not a document defect).** The source's own rule sentence — "The points the site meters are counted as the metered points that posted a reading in the month ending on the day of the amendment, one reading to a point." — does not name a reading source; only the private compute binding does (`reading_source='interval_meter'`). The published document carries that sentence exactly as the source states it, so the KB is faithful. Where the source leaves a boundary open in prose the documents may not close it, and they have not. I record the openness against the policy side: the same phrase in `energy_ext_meter_coverage_amendment`'s rule and in the `portfolio_band` factor would, on a record that also carries a utility-bill reading in the window, admit a second count. In this task the alternative reading is additionally excluded on the visible surface, because at 35 covered points the coverage-share rule ("at or above the included count | fewer than the points covered | 95 percent") would have to be taken and the corpus's own reading-source discipline elsewhere ("The readings counted are those posted from the interval meters") makes the interval reading the natural one.

All three prerequisite hops were **state-derived**; none was pre-solved, so nothing carries into the dependency-form scan from this task.
